findings.evidence: Mathlib/Logic/Equiv/Basic.lean:262 defines `Equiv.subtypeEquiv`; Mathlib/Combinatorics/Configuration.lean:188 demonstrates `(Equiv.prodComm _ _).subtypeEquiv`, while `YoungDiagram.mem_transpose` supplies exactly the required predicate equivalence.
findings.fix: Define it with `(Equiv.prodComm ℕ ℕ).subtypeEquiv (fun c => YoungDiagram.mem_transpose)` (adjusting orientation with `.symm` if needed).
findings.issue: `transposeCellEquiv` manually rebuilds the restriction of product commutation to the two cell subtypes.

findings.evidence: Mathlib/Logic/Equiv/Defs.lean:252 defines the `[simp]` theorem `Equiv.symm_apply_apply`; the submitted proof is directly `(transposeEquiv μ).left_inv T`.
findings.fix: Remove this declaration and use `(transposeEquiv μ).symm_apply_apply T`; `transposeEquiv_apply` rewrites the forward application to `T.transpose` when necessary.
findings.issue: `transposeEquiv_symm_transpose` is exactly the generic inverse-after-forward theorem for `transposeEquiv`.

summary: The tableau construction is new, but two pieces duplicate generic Mathlib equivalence infrastructure.
